I collect seeds everywhere I go and have ended up with more than I can handle. Between my small container patio garden, and a little urban raised bed, I just can't support the sized garden I want while living in the city. This leaves me with a lot of excess!

I currently have seeds for: Laos Chilis, Lufa Gourd, Laos Pumpkin, Thai Chilis, decorative corn, Chinese Noodle Beans (long beans), bush green beans, some fuzzy cucumber that looks sort of like a big kiwi, kale, and spinach. I also have pumpkin seeds that got all mixed together, but are from pumpkin pie and albino/white varieties. Aside from the spinach and kale, all of these do best in zones 8b or warmer, needing relatively long growing seasons.

I have tangerine seeds from Puebla, Mexico, and am skeptical about how well these will do at sea level. If anyone has any suggestions about starting citrus from seed (I know it's not usually a fruitful endeavor), please let me know!

The laos chili and pumpkin seeds I actually did get in Laos, along with the chinese long beans and thai chilis. Southern Louisiana has a similar climate/rainy season so these varietals do well here.
